request.text:
The only road to the crater crosses the canyon, and the only bridge belongs to a goblin called Vorga. He took it in spring.
<long pause>
His Host lets the Scarwalker caravans over to the wells, then keeps the water. A toll, he calls it. The elder has another word.
<long pause>
Yes, he's one of Vorga's. Yes, he's a guest. No, you can't. Let the poor thing finish his tea.
<long pause>
Young, loud, very fond of his own voice. He sends the Scarwalkers a song every new moon about how he's going to eat them.
<long pause>
Terrible song. Good rhythm, though. And under all the shouting, he's angrier than anyone I've ever met.
<long pause>
He knows. He's telling the whole canyon she sold the clan for a few sacks of grain, and that you're holding the leash.
<long pause>
The lads who fought you at the ford were his. The ones who made it home haven't stopped talking about you.
<long pause>
He knows. He doesn't sing about the Scarwalkers any more. All the new verses are about you.
<long pause>
Whatever he thought of her, she was his grandmother. Nobody else was allowed to kill her.
<long pause>
He says Vorga will be delighted to meet you. He says to bring rope. He seems to think that's funny.
<long pause>
A Kindled caravan, nine days ago, under a white cloth. The elder gave them water, because the law says she must.
<long pause>
Their leader asked after you by name. Lovely voice. Kind eyes. I didn't like how much I liked her.
<long pause>
No. A clan has grandmothers. Vorga's Host is everyone who got tired of waiting for the grandmothers.
<long pause>
Anything else, before the tea runs out?
<long pause>
Nothing in the Sunscar would dare touch you tonight. Tomorrow is another song.
<long pause>
That's the verse before the last. I've been looking for it for twenty years.
<long pause>
Seven came home, my version goes. Hers says they came back running. Same seven, I'd wager, seen from different doorsteps.
<long pause>
Of course not. I'd keep it too, if it were mine.
<long pause>
Then someone else will want very badly to hear that dream. Be careful who you tell it to.
<long pause>
Big promise. Goblins remember promises. So do songs.
<long pause>
Honest. I think she'll like that better than a promise.
<long pause>
Every Warden song I know ends at a door like this. None of them say what's behind it. That ought to worry me more.
